notes:
Top-level: building a commercial VS Code extension for teams and freelancers. Primary ask: low-latency inline suggestions (ideally <=60ms median) and streaming completions that update the editor as tokens arrive. CTO quote on 2026-02-14 call: "No user code leaves our stack without per-repo consent; must support allowlist/blocklist and on-prem option later."

POC goals: integrate Redwood streaming API into extension background service, demonstrate model-version pinning so customers can opt into newer model families, show rate-limit tiers (free/dev/pro) and graceful degradation to cached suggestions.

Technical notes: extension uses WebSocket fallback for streaming, expects prefix caching for tokens, wants an SDK method to commit KV cache between sessions. Concern about tokenization differences between local editor heuristics and server model; asked for guidance on deterministic tokenizer pairing.

Commercial: mid-market budget but high sensitivity to per-1000-token costs; interested in Optimize recommendations to tune batching/quantization for common JS/TS completion workloads.

Sales snippets: "Wants 7-day POC starting Mar 15", "Legal wants data residency options for EU customers", "If POC meets latency and security requirements, forecast to close Apr 2026 (50-150k ARR)."
